Sign up for free here to receive this newsletter in your inbox every Saturday. You’ll also get our weekly newsletter with an exclusive introduction from our editor-in-chief. A boyfriend I had at university in Tokyo once told me that older teammates from his sports club had taken him to a sex parlour. So I was not surprised to learn that 48% of Japanese men have paid for sex at some point, compared with 11% of British men. In Japan the industry is woven into male social life—but it has rarely been the subject of serious debate, and the laws governing it are murky. This year, though, sex work became a political issue. The trigger was a rise in street prostitution around a park in Tokyo. It stands out in a country where most of the trade happens behind closed doors. Nor has it helped that many of the men approaching these women are foreign tourists taking advantage of a weak yen. For some Japanese men—even those who think nothing of buying sex themselves—that stings their pride. In the booming 1970s and 80s, it was Japanese men who flew abroad for it. 76648.body:

Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** Claude found weaknesses in encryption that human experts missed for years, and 1,132 of the people building frontier AI asked Washington to slow their own employers down. Meanwhile Trump closed the border to Chinese robots and Microsoft unveiled an AI that plays attacker and defender at the same time.



**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Anthropic:** Is Mythos really that good?

* **The letter:** Why did OpenAI and Anthropic employees ask the USA to slow their companies down?

* **Trump:** Which Chinese machines just got banned?

* **Microsoft:** Why does its new AI attack the people it protects?


----------



----------
## [Mythos poked holes in unbreakable encryption](https://www.anthropic.com/research/discovering-cryptographic-weaknesses)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7fc42b99-f810-44a8-aaa3-a508eda6bfb3/Beehiiv_01_-_Jul_29.png?t=1785319132)
Caption: 

Encryption is the math keeping your bank login and your messages private, and it holds for one reason. The world's best mathematicians attack it for years and come up empty.

Anthropic pointed Claude Mythos at two of its most studied pieces, and Mythos found gaps in both.

HAWK is a signature scheme built to survive quantum computers. Human experts reviewed it for two years and passed it twice, and Mythos cut its strength in half in 60 hours.

It also made the best-known attack on a weakened version of AES, the cipher behind most internet traffic, 200 to 800 times faster.

Claude turned the AES job down at first, insisting there was nothing left to find. Three days of pep talks and a billion tokens later, it had the attack.

Plenty of ciphers guarding real systems have had far less review than these two, and Anthropic's own researchers needed a month to verify a week of Claude's work.

Nothing you use today breaks. Both were research targets.

76647.subject: Turn Claude Opus 5 Into a Financial Analyst That Never Sleeps 📊
76647.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/claude-opus-5-financial-analyst

👋 Hey, Linas here! Every day, I break down 3 stories shaping the future of FinTech & Artificial Intelligence - plus the money movements and trends worth tracking. First time here? 398k+ FinTech and AI leaders get this daily. Join them:
A first-year investment banking analyst costs north of $200,000 fully loaded. Claude Opus 5, released seven days ago, runs a complete DCF valuation for roughly the price of a coffee ☕
On Finance Agent v2, the benchmark run by independent evaluator Vals AI over 927 expert-reviewed questions on real public company filings, Opus 5 now ranks first at 58.63%, ahead of Gemini 3.5 Flash (57.86%) and Muse Spark 1.1 (57.21%). On the stricter all-pass metric, where every sub-question must be right, Opus 5 hits 47.71% while every other model stays below 46%.
That is a genuine #1, and it is scored by someone other than Anthropic. So it’s a really solid AI model.
Now read the same result the other way, because the other way is what determines whether it works for you.
58.63% means roughly two out of five analyst tasks still come back wrong. The lead over second place is just 0.77 percentage points, and on the all-pass metric even the best model fails more than half of entry-level tasks outright.
Thus, Opus 5 is the best drafting AI engine in finance that anyone has independently measured, and it is nowhere near an unattended oracle. The framework below is built for exactly that gap. It gets maximum leverage out of the draft while making every assumption visible enough to review fast.
What Actually Changed in Opus 5
Let’s be precise about which capabilities matter for financial work.
It tops the finance leaderboards, but it is not the frontier model. Beyond Finance Agent v2, Vals AI ranks Opus 5 first on CorpFin v2 (73.19%), MortgageTax (72.06%), SWE-bench Verified (97.00%), MMLU Pro (91.59%), MMMU (89.88%), and Code Migration (57.47%). It is not first on GPQA Diamond (93.43%, fourth) or Terminal-Bench 2.1 (84.64%, second), and on Vals’ composite index it sits second at 74.82%, behind Claude Fable 5 [ https://substack.com/redirect/ece565db-258f-492d-895c-4634c3f051b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] at 75.14%.
Know the weak spots too. Opus 5 ranks 18th of 20 on CyberBench (40.68%) and, more relevant for finance, 18th of 132 on TaxEval v2. Thus, it’s strong at modelling, distinctly average at tax.
There is also a tooling nuance behind that #1. Vals’ Finance Agent v2 gives its agents only generic tools: SEC EDGAR search, web search, page parsing, a calculator, and historical price data, with no Excel and no licensed data feeds. So that #1 was earned reading raw filings unaided, which cuts both ways. The ceiling should definitely be higher with real data infrastructure behind it; it also means the benchmark is not measuring the stack you would actually deploy.
